tagline: Access to Justice Begins with Access to the Path

roadmap.title: Judicial Career Roadmap
roadmap.click_for_details: Click on any step to view details

step1_desc: Completing Class 12 is the foundational step. Students from any stream (Science, Commerce, or Arts) can pursue law. Focus on developing strong English and reasoning skills.
step2_desc: Prepare for and clear entrance exams like CLAT (Common Law Admission Test), AILET (All India Law Entrance Test), or State-level CETs. These scores determine your admission into top National Law Universities (NLUs) and other reputed law colleges.
step3_desc: Enroll in a 5-year integrated LLB course (after Class 12) or a 3-year LLB course (after graduation). This is a mandatory requirement to become a lawyer or a judge. Focus on core subjects like Constitutional Law, IPC, CrPC, CPC, and Evidence Act.
step4_desc: After completing LLB, it is highly recommended (and sometimes mandatory for Higher Judicial Services) to practice as an advocate in District or High Courts. This gives you practical exposure to court proceedings and case handling.
step5_desc: This is the most critical step. Appear for the State Judicial Services Examination (PCS-J) conducted by respective State Public Service Commissions or High Courts. The exam typically consists of three stages: Preliminary (Objective), Mains (Subjective), and Interview (Personality Test).
step6_desc: Once selected, you will undergo rigorous training at a Judicial Academy. This training covers procedural laws, judgment writing, and court administration, preparing you for the bench.
step7_desc: Upon successful completion of training, you will be appointed as a Civil Judge (Junior Division) or Judicial Magistrate. This marks the beginning of your illustrious career in the Indian Judiciary.
